title: Tenant-scoped RBAC provisioning and evidence pipeline for SSO/SCIM compliance
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Goal: Provide tenant-scoped access controls and a provable, automatable evidence pipeline that satisfies auditors for SSO/SAML + SCIM onboarding, periodic access review, and data residency-bound retention policies.

Scope:
- RBAC model: tenant -> environment -> role (fine-grained, hierarchical).
- SCIM provisioning enhancements: maintain authoritative group->role mappings; support one-way and two-way sync modes; track delta snapshots for attestations.
- SAML mapping: canonical attribute mapping and fallback for multiple IdPs per tenant.
- Periodic access reviews: scheduled attestation flows with reviewer handoffs and automated reminders; capture decisions as signed artifacts.
- Evidence pipeline: automated export of attestation events + SCIM sync deltas + role-change audit trail, signed and archived with residency metadata.
- Integration with retention settings and residency enforcement: evidence artifacts respect tenant retention and residency settings (region tag + TTL).

Success criteria / Acceptance criteria:
1) New tenant onboarding flow can bind multiple IdPs and map SAML groups to RD roles; when enabled, SCIM provisioning can create/update users and groups with the correct role assignments.
2) Attestation job produces an evidence bundle for a tenant that includes: SCIM snapshot (pre/post), role-change events, SAML assertion logs for the period, and reviewer decisions; bundle is cryptographically signed and stored in the tenant's allowed residency region.
3) Evidence export API returns tamper-evident JSONL with residency metadata; support for retrieval by compliance team and export to third-party evidence store.
4) Periodic access review UI/flow in Console shows reviewer assignments, outcomes, and automatically triggers remediation tasks for revoked access.
5) End-to-end latency for authorization checks remains < 15ms for cached lookups and < 60ms for cold-policy evaluation on the critical path.
6) Migration path for existing >= 95% of active tenants without forcing immediate re-provisioning; fallback compatibility layer for legacy flat roles.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Chosen hierarchical RBAC (tenant->env->role) to limit complexity when mapping many IdP groups; trade-off: slightly more complex policy evaluation logic.
- Enforce policy at the gateway with a local policy cache and short TTL (30s) to reduce network calls; trade-off: brief window where newly-revoked access may persist until cache invalidation. Mitigation: immediate invalidation on critical revocations and consumer-facing session kill endpoints.
- SCIM will record deltas (before/after) and we will persist only the deltas + computed snapshot per evidence retention rule to avoid unbounded storage growth.
- Evidence artifacts are signed using the platform HSM-backed key and include residency tag and retention expiry; signatures provide tamper-evidence for auditors.

Implementation plan (phase breakdown):
- Phase 1 (Q1): Schema + API for tenant role model, SCIM delta capture hooks, SAML attribute mapping layer.
- Phase 2 (Q2): Attestation engine to assemble evidence bundles, signing integration, residency tagging, storage adapters (S3 in region, on-prem export).
- Phase 3 (Q3): Console flows for periodic access reviews and automated remediation; telemetry and latency optimizations.

Migration and rollback:
- Default to compatibility mode for existing tenants; provide opt-in migration tool that computes expected post-migration role assignments and a dry-run evidence bundle.
- Rollback via control-plane flags to revert to flat-role enforcement for tenants that need more time.

QA & testing:
- Fuzz tests for SCIM deltas and group->role resolution to catch edge cases with nested groups.
- Property tests for signature verification and residency tag enforcement.
- End-to-end integration tests with a simulated IdP (SAML) and SCIM client.

Documentation & compliance artifacts:
- Confluence design: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/COMP/Tenant+RBAC+and+Evidence+Pipeline (draft)
- Sample attestation artifact schema: signed-jsonl-v1 (attached in evidence_artifacts)

Rollout:
- Canary rollout to 5% of new tenants on dedicated infra; gather telemetry for authorization latency and evidence generation times.
- After canary validation, gradual enablement for existing tenants with migration tooling and a 30-day opt-out window.
